t: Harun al-Rashid became caliph in 786, in his early twenties, with the help of his mother al-Khayzuran and of Yahya ibn Khalid the Barmakid, whose family then ran the administration for seventeen years.
Under him the Abbasid empire reached its peak and Baghdad flourished, while he fought Byzantium, exchanged embassies with Charlemagne and put down Kharijite and Alid revolts.
He destroyed the Barmakids, imprisoned Alid leaders, and divided the succession between his sons al-Amin and al-Ma'mun, who went to war after his death.
dyk: In 802 Harun sent Charlemagne an elephant named Abul-Abbas and a water clock that marked the hours by dropping bronze balls into a bowl while mechanical knights, one for each hour, came out of little doors. Charlemagne and his retinue took the clock for a conjuration.
ev: Harun nominally leads an expedition against the Byzantines that reaches the Asian suburbs of Constantinople, and is given the name al-Rashid
On the death of his brother al-Hadi he becomes the fifth Abbasid caliph, with Yahya ibn Khalid the Barmakid as vizier
The Alid Yahya ibn Abdallah proclaims a revolt in Daylam, and Harun has his son Muhammad sworn in as heir with the name al-Amin
He moves the court and government from Baghdad to Raqqa on the middle Euphrates
He recognises Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab as semi-autonomous emir of Ifriqiya in exchange for an annual payment
He sends Charlemagne an elephant and a water clock, and the new Byzantine emperor Nikephoros I refuses him tribute
By al-Tabari's dating, he has Ja'far the Barmakid executed and the rest of the family imprisoned
He dies at Tus in Khorasan while marching against the rebel Rafi ibn al-Layth, and al-Amin succeeds him

f.born: Between 763 and 766 (17 March 763 and February 766 are the most probable dates), at Rey in Jibal, in present-day Iran; son of the Abbasid caliph al-Mahdi and al-Khayzuran
f.died: 24 March 809, of an illness, at Sanabad village in Tus, Khorasan, while marching against the rebel Rafi ibn al-Layth; buried there in the Dar al-Imarah
f.role: Nominal leader of campaigns against the Byzantines, 780 and 782; crown prince and governor of the empire's western territories, from Syria to Azerbaijan; fifth Abbasid caliph, September 786 – March 809
f.known: A reign traditionally seen as the start of the Islamic Golden Age; the Bayt al-Hikma ("House of Wisdom") in Baghdad; campaigns against Byzantium; the exchange of embassies and gifts with Charlemagne; the fall of the Barmakids; his place in the One Thousand and One Nights
